why: All moves cost 1 second, so the fastest way to the bottom-right corner is the BFS shortest path on the grid graph; compare that distance with maxTime.
hints: Every step costs the same. Which search gives shortest paths in an unweighted graph?
Run BFS from (0,0) over '.' cells with 4-directional moves; the first time you reach the bottom-right cell you have the minimum time.
Queue plus a visited/distance grid, O(rows * cols). Answer 'Yes' if the distance exists and is <= maxTime.
pitfalls: Unreachable target means 'No', not an exception.
A 1x1 grid needs 0 seconds, so it is 'Yes' even with maxTime 0.
Mark cells visited when you push them, not when you pop, or the queue can grow very large on a 500x500 grid.
